design.declaration: application.Builder.SPA(id, assets foundation.Key[*http.Assets], config http.SPAConfig) snapshots the configuration and registers http.RegisterSPA on application.RouterKey. http.RegisterSPA is the owner: it validates the route ID and configuration at registration, contributes to the router's collection and resolves the assets key when the router factory runs during Build, then applies Router.WithSPA.
design.validation: Build constructs services before any provider boots, so an unknown assets key (fault.Missing), invalid configuration (fault.Invalid) and a route ID or prefix repeating another SPA or declared route (fault.Duplicate) fail before asset directories open.
design.composition: A router view with SPAs attaches them to the request context. An asset mount defers to the most specific SPA covering the path whose prefix is at least as specific as its own: a more specific SPA owns its subtree (what it declines is 404, never a lookup in the outer mount); an equal one answers the mount's misses. Declared routes and more specific mounts match first natively and keep their own 404s.
design.unchanged: Router.WithSPA's native-miss fallback, exclusions, HTML-navigation rules, prefix redirect, SPAConfig.CacheControl, route inspection metadata and contract export.

checks.mutations: Removing the context hand-off, the more specific SPA's ownership, the equal-prefix miss hand-off or the contribution application failed 12, 1, 3 and 14 fixture subtests respectively

limits: When an SPA is more specific than a matching mount, the SPA's response runs inside that mount's route middleware.

The starter change itself (bumping the pin and switching PortalRoutes to Builder.SPA) is out of scope; it can either drop its /admin mount (the SPA serves existing files) or keep it (the equal-prefix SPA answers its misses).
